title: Scorpions Reschedule 2026 Mexico Shows and Las Vegas Residency for 2027
content:
Archive note: This English edition follows Oldies Radyo’s report of 4 September 2026. Dates and announced plans reflect the information available when that report was written.

Scorpions have moved their Mexico concerts and eight-night Las Vegas residency to 2027. The German rock veterans cited unforeseen circumstances but offered no further explanation for the postponement.

September shows pushed back a year

The change affects three Mexican dates and an eight-show Las Vegas run that had been scheduled for September 2026.

Organisers attributed the postponement to unforeseen circumstances. No new, verified information about the band members’ health accompanied the announcement, so there is no basis for speculation about the reasons behind the decision.

The rescheduled dates

Scorpions are now due to return to Mexico on August 27, 2027, in Zapopan, followed by Mexico City on August 30 and Monterrey on September 2.

Their Coming Home Las Vegas residency will take place at PH Live at Planet Hollywood from September 9 to 25, 2027. The eight shows are scheduled for September 9, 11, 14, 16, 18, 21, 23 and 25.

The band also confirmed plans to continue the Coming Home – 60 Years of Scorpions tour in 2027, with further European dates to be announced.

A longer wait for fans

With songs such as “Rock You Like a Hurricane”, “Still Loving You” and “Wind of Change” connecting generations of listeners, Scorpions are not calling time on live performance. The new dates point to a return to these stages roughly a year later than planned.

The Oldies Radyo take: Waiting another year for a Scorpions show will test fans’ patience, but sometimes even rock ’n’ roll has to take its time. For now, the dates are in the 2027 calendar, and attention turns to the band’s next announcement.

title: Oasis Reunion Documentary Don’t Look Back in Anger Premieres in Venice
content:
Archive note: This English edition follows Oldies Radyo’s report of 5 September 2026. Dates and announced plans reflect the information available when that report was written.

One of the defining music stories of the 1990s has found its way to the big screen. Liam and Noel Gallagher attended the Venice Film Festival on September 5 for the world premiere of Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger, a documentary tracing the band’s reunion.

A rock-star arrival in Venice

The Gallagher brothers arrived by water taxi, greeting the crowds waiting for them. Liam described the Venice atmosphere as “biblical” in his unmistakable style, while Noel kept his response brief and Italian: “Bellissimo.”

More than a concert film

Directed by Dylan Southern and Will Lovelace, the documentary looks beyond the spectacle of Oasis’s comeback shows. It follows the band’s return and the brothers’ gradual reconciliation, 16 years after the backstage row in Paris that brought Oasis to an end in 2009.

Previously unseen rehearsal footage, backstage material and the brothers’ first joint interview in roughly 25 years are among the film’s highlights.

The cameras stay with the band from the earliest rehearsals through the world tour’s vast stadium shows. Rather than steering events, the directors chose to observe Liam and Noel as the distance between them began to close.

From the 1990s to a new generation

Formed in Manchester in 1991, Oasis became the sound of an era with Definitely Maybe and (What’s the Story) Morning Glory?, their influence reaching well beyond Britpop.

“Wonderwall”, “Live Forever”, “Don’t Look Back in Anger” and “Champagne Supernova” continued to find listeners long after the band split in 2009. When the reunion tour opened in Cardiff in 2025, tens of thousands of fans from different generations gathered in front of the same stage — a reminder of how deeply those songs still resonate.

Steven Knight, who is credited with the documentary’s screenplay, describes a story rooted in reconciliation, forgiveness and brotherhood, as well as the return of a major rock band.

In cinemas on September 11

Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger is scheduled to open in selected cinemas and IMAX venues on September 11. A Disney+ release is also planned for later in the year.

The Oldies Radyo take: The Oasis reunion is a reminder that songs can outlast even the bands that made them. Liam and Noel may have spent years apart, but “Live Forever” and “Don’t Look Back in Anger” kept connecting millions of listeners throughout that silence.

title: Stevie Wonder Announces 50th Anniversary Tour for Songs in the Key of Life
content:
Archive note: This English edition follows Oldies Radyo’s report of 9 September 2026. Dates and announced plans reflect the information available when that report was written.

Stevie Wonder is preparing to celebrate the 50th anniversary of his 1976 masterpiece Songs in the Key of Life with a special concert series. The legendary artist will perform the album in full across 18 shows in Europe and the United States.

A Masterpiece Returns to the Stage 50 Years Later

The tour, titled Songs in the Key of Life Performances – 50th Anniversary Tour, will begin in Birmingham on October 13, 2026. Shows in Paris, Copenhagen, Oslo, Stockholm, Hanover, Cologne and Amsterdam will be followed by concerts in Dublin, London, Manchester and Glasgow.

The U.S. leg includes Madison Square Garden in New York, the United Center in Chicago, Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C., and two nights in Stevie Wonder’s hometown of Detroit. The concert series is scheduled to conclude on December 19 at the Intuit Dome in Los Angeles.

From “Sir Duke” to “Isn’t She Lovely”

Songs in the Key of Life is widely regarded as one of the greatest commercial and artistic achievements of Stevie Wonder’s career. The album includes enduring songs such as “Sir Duke,” “I Wish,” “As,” “Pastime Paradise” and “Isn’t She Lovely.”

In addition to producing the album, Wonder wrote and arranged much of the material and played numerous instruments on the recordings. Musicians including Herbie Hancock, George Benson and Minnie Riperton also contributed to the project.

The album won Album of the Year at the 1977 Grammy Awards. After selling more than 10 million copies worldwide and earning diamond certification, it was also added to the U.S. Library of Congress National Recording Registry for its cultural and historical significance.

The Songs Still Feel Current

Half a century after the album’s release, its themes of love, solidarity, justice and social unity remain strikingly relevant. Wonder’s decision to perform the record in full makes the tour more than a nostalgic anniversary celebration.

Audiences will hear not only a collection of major hits, but also the larger story the album tells from beginning to end. The tour will also be Wonder’s first extensive concert series since the 2024 Sing Your Song! As We Fix Our Nation’s Broken Heart run.

Oldies Radyo’s take: Some albums remain memories of their era; others grow more meaningful as the years pass. Songs in the Key of Life belongs to the second group, continuing to speak about humanity, love and the hope for a better world. Hearing these songs again in Stevie Wonder’s own voice 50 years later is a reminder that music history is still very much alive.

title: U2 Named 2027 MusiCares Persons of the Year
content:
Archive note: This English edition follows Oldies Radyo’s report of 11 September 2026. Dates and announced plans reflect the information available when that report was written.

U2 will be honored by MusiCares for nearly 50 years of music and humanitarian work around the world. At a special event in Los Angeles, artists from different generations will perform some of the band’s most memorable songs.

U2 Honored for Music and Solidarity

One of rock history’s biggest bands, U2 has been named the 2027 MusiCares Persons of the Year. Bono, The Edge, Adam Clayton and Larry Mullen Jr. will be honored at a benefit gala at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on February 5, 2027.

MusiCares cited not only U2’s musical legacy, but also the group’s long-running work in areas including global health, disaster relief, addiction recovery, mental health and access to music education.

Artists Will Perform U2 Songs

The event, one of Grammy Week’s major annual gatherings, will feature artists from different generations performing songs from U2’s catalog. The performers will be announced at a later date.

Proceeds from the evening will support MusiCares programs that assist music professionals facing health problems or personal and financial hardship.

For the first time in the organization’s 36-year history, individual tickets will also be sold for the concert portion of the event, allowing music fans outside the traditional invited tables to attend the tribute to U2.

Nearly 50 Years from Dublin to the World

Formed in Dublin in 1976, U2 became part of the shared musical memory of several generations with songs including “Sunday Bloody Sunday,” “Pride (In the Name of Love),” “With or Without You,” “Where the Streets Have No Name” and “One.”

Especially during the 1980s and 1990s, the band became known for combining stadium-scale rock, powerful visual storytelling and engagement with social issues. Bono was previously named MusiCares Person of the Year as an individual in 2003. This time, the honor goes to all four members of the band together.

Oldies Radyo’s take: U2’s story is about more than major albums and packed concerts. For nearly half a century, the band has kept reminding audiences that music can speak up in the face of the world’s problems. This honor recognizes not only what U2 achieved on stage, but also the mark the band has left beyond it.

title: Madonna Returns to the VMAs Stage After 23 Years as Nirvana Receives Video Vanguard Award
content:
Archive note: This English edition follows Oldies Radyo’s report of 21 September 2026. Dates and announced plans reflect the information available when that report was written.

The MTV Video Music Awards will bring together two defining legacies of pop and rock history on September 27. Madonna will return to open the VMAs for the first time in 23 years, while Nirvana will be honored with the Video Vanguard Award.

Madonna Makes a Major VMA Comeback

Madonna last opened the VMAs in 2003. Over the years, she has delivered some of the most talked-about moments in MTV history, including her 1984 performance of “Like a Virgin” and her 1990 rendition of “Vogue.”

Her opening performance at the September 27 ceremony will mark a return to one of music television’s most iconic stages.

Nirvana’s Visual Legacy Honored

Nirvana’s Video Vanguard Award recognizes the band’s impact not only on music, but also on the language of the music video. “Smells Like Teen Spirit” became one of the era’s most influential visual statements, carrying the mood of 1990s youth culture around the world in just a few minutes.

The legacy created by Kurt Cobain, Krist Novoselic and Dave Grohl played a defining role both in bringing grunge into the mainstream and in increasing the visibility of alternative music on television.

Two Major Names in MTV History

Madonna’s return to the stage and Nirvana’s recognition give the VMA ceremony a significance that goes beyond the year’s current nominees. The pop revolution of the 1980s and the alternative-rock explosion of the 1990s will once again share the same program.

Taylor Swift will also receive the inaugural Artist Director Honors award. For Oldies Radyo, however, the night’s strongest nostalgic weight lies in Madonna’s return and in the renewed recognition of Nirvana’s influence across generations.

From Oldies Radyo

Some artists are remembered for their songs; others for the way the atmosphere changes the moment they step onto a stage. Madonna and Nirvana were two of the strongest symbols of the years when MTV was not simply a music channel, but a stage that helped shape popular culture.
